QF.id: Concept and Role of Mutual Fund_22

question.text: A mutual fund scheme has 10 crore units outstanding with a face value of Rs. 10 per unit. The current NAV of the scheme is Rs. 25 per unit. What is the AUM (Assets Under Management) of this scheme?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per pages 39-40 of the workbook, AUM = Current NAV per unit x Total outstanding units. Here, AUM = Rs. 25 x 10 crore units = Rs. 250 crore. The face value (Rs. 10) is used to compute the Unit Capital, not the AUM. The Trap: Option B (Rs. 100 crore) is what you get if you wrongly use face value (Rs. 10) instead of NAV (Rs. 25) — this yields Unit Capital. Option C (Rs. 150 crore) is the difference between AUM and Unit Capital, not AUM itself. Option D (Rs. 350 crore) wrongly adds face value to NAV before multiplying. Note: Always distinguish between Unit Capital (Face Value x Units) and AUM (NAV x Units); the AUM uses the current NAV.
